concepts.name: Database Transaction
concepts.description: Grouping several statements into one atomic unit that commits together or rolls back together, so a failure never leaves partial writes.
concepts.context: transfer() in app/transfers.py wraps the debit, credit and ledger insert in `with conn:` so an exception rolls all three back

concepts.name: Connection Context Manager
concepts.description: Python's sqlite3 connection used as a context manager commits on a clean exit and rolls back on an exception; it does not close the connection.
concepts.context: `with conn:` at the top of transfer() in app/transfers.py turns InsufficientFunds into a rollback instead of a commit

concepts.name: Atomicity
concepts.description: The all-or-nothing guarantee of a transaction: either every step of an operation takes effect or none does.
concepts.context: The debit UPDATE, credit UPDATE and ledger INSERT in transfer() must succeed together, or money would vanish or appear

concepts.name: Check-Then-Act Race
concepts.description: A race where a condition is read and acted on in separate steps, so another writer can change the data in between and invalidate the check.
concepts.context: transfer() SELECTs the balance and compares it to cents before the UPDATE; two concurrent transfers can both pass the check and overdraw the account

concepts.name: Parameterized Queries
concepts.description: Passing values separately from the SQL text through placeholders so input is never interpolated into the statement, preventing SQL injection.
concepts.context: Every conn.execute in app/transfers.py uses `?` placeholders with a tuple of (cents, src, dst) rather than f-strings

concepts.name: Ledger Audit Trail
concepts.description: Recording each money movement as an append-only row so balances can be audited and reconciled against the history.
concepts.context: The INSERT INTO ledger (src, dst, cents) in transfer() is committed in the same transaction as the balance updates so the log always matches the balances

concepts.name: Integer Money
concepts.description: Storing currency as integer minor units such as cents instead of floats, to avoid rounding errors in arithmetic and comparison.
concepts.context: transfer() takes `cents` as an integer and compares and subtracts it directly against the balance column, avoiding float drift
